instructions_to_main_agent: CRITICAL: You MUST use plain CSS and React only. DO NOT install or use Tailwind CSS, Shadcn, or any UI frameworks.
Write pure CSS classes in src/index.css and apply them via className in .jsx files.
Keep all existing CSS variables intact and use them exclusively for colors.
Adhere strictly to the requested layouts and functionalities. DO NOT alter the existing color palette.
You have .js or .jsx files, do not use TypeScript (.tsx).

rules: Headings use Fraunces, giving a classic, editorial finance feel.
Body text uses IBM Plex Sans for functional clarity.
Numbers, data points, statuses, and JSON logs MUST use JetBrains Mono.

css_classes_to_create..text-h1: font-family: Fraunces, serif; font-size: clamp(2.5rem, 5vw, 4rem); letter-spacing: -0.02em; line-height: 1.1; font-weight: 300;
css_classes_to_create..text-h2: font-family: Fraunces, serif; font-size: 2rem; letter-spacing: -0.01em; line-height: 1.2; font-weight: 400;
css_classes_to_create..text-body: font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--text);

colors.instructions: Use ONLY these CSS variables. Do not use hex codes directly.

structure: Hero Section: Immersive full height, background image with heavy dark gradient overlay (background: linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(11,13,16,0.6), var(--bg))). Massive Fraunces H1: 'The AI Purchasing Agent for Finance'. Accent button 'Enter App'.
How It Works Grid: A CSS grid displaying 4 core features (Quote Parsing, Policy Checks, Virtual Cards, Auto-Approvals) with plain CSS cards (.surface-card).
Top Nav: Brand name (Fraunces) and 'Run History'.
Main Split View (.grid-split): Left column for 'New Purchase' form. Right column for 'Run History' list.
New Purchase Form: Shows a mock vendor quote email, spending policy rules, and an approval mode toggle (I approve each one / auto answers). 'Start Agent' button.
Run History List: Rows of past runs displaying Vendor, Plan, Status, Card State. Include checkboxes to select exactly 2 runs for comparison. 'Compare Selected' button appears when 2 are selected.
Three-pane layout using CSS Grid (.layout-3-pane: grid-template-columns: 250px 1fr 320px; gap: 2rem; align-items: start;).
Left Pane (Sticky): 'Scene Jump Menu' - list of 8 chapters. Highlights the active chapter currently playing.

Middle Pane: 'Live Stream Timeline'. Rendered grouped by chapter. Each chapter has a Plain-language title (Fraunces), a one-line explanation, and the original scene title (Mono, dimmed). Timeline events stream in beneath.

Right Pane (Sticky): 'Context Panel'. Contains Approval actions (only visible when a charge exceeds policy or price rises), Virtual Card visualization, and Cash Forecast Chart (Recharts). Tabs for Timeline / Raw JSON.
Top Bar: Back button to /app, Title 'Comparing Runs'.
Each Column: Displays the timeline, chosen plan, approvals asked, and card limits for that run. Use a subtle var(--surface-2) background on rows that represent differences between the runs.

components.LiveTimeline: Use a vertical line on the left (border-left: 1px solid var(--line)). Events are placed with relative positioning. Animate new events with opacity and transform (translateY).
components.SceneJumpMenu: A list of anchor links acting as a table of contents. Inactive links use var(--dim). Active link uses color: var(--accent) and border-left: 2px solid var(--accent).
components.VirtualCard: A container simulating a credit card. padding: 1.5rem; border-radius: 12px; background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--surface-2), var(--surface)); border: 1px solid var(--line). Display limit in mono. If frozen, add box-shadow: 0 0 15px rgba(142, 155, 255, 0.3) and border-color: var(--frozen).
components.ApprovalPanel: If status is 'waiting for human', show a card with 'Approve' (.btn-ok) and 'Decline' (.btn-bad) buttons.
components.ForecastChart: Use Recharts LineChart. Line stroke=var(--text). Add a ReferenceLine at y=25000 (Reserve Floor) colored var(--bad).
components.Card/Surface: .surface-card { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px; padding: 1.5rem; }

rules: Use specific transitions: transition: transform 0.2s ease, opacity 0.2s ease, background-color 0.2s ease, border-color 0.2s ease.
Button hover: transform: translateY(-1px); filter: brightness(1.1);
Live Streaming: When a new event arrives, apply an entrance animation. @keyframes slideIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } }
All buttons/links MUST have clear focus outlines (outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px).
Include data-testid on all interactive and key informational elements (e.g., data-testid='approve-button', data-testid='jump-link-1').
Ensure text contrast against var(--surface) meets WCAG AA.

image_urls.description: Futuristic graphs and abstract dark data interface.
image_urls.instructions: Use as a background image on the hero section with a heavy dark overlay so text remains highly readable.

general_ui_ux_design_guidelines: Optical alignment over geometrical alignment. Adjust paddings visually.
Generous Spacing: Use rem units for spacing. Avoid cramped UI (e.g., gap: 2rem).
Do NOT center align the app container. Content should be left-aligned for a technical, precise feel.
Use layered z-index hierarchy. --bg is base, --surface is elevated, --surface-2 is top level.
Never use purely transparent backgrounds on floating elements or dropdowns; use var(--surface) with a var(--line) border.
Buttons should be modern, pill-shaped or slightly rounded, utilizing var(--accent) for primary actions.
